answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use a lineage bond: each identity carries a signed relic from a one-time, costly registration and locks a ferrous stake that is slashed for double-spending or forking its name. Reward and voting weight grow with the age and bonded size of that relic, so splitting into many wallets resets the clock and makes each shard post its own bond. An attacker pays the mint fee and collateral for every fake relic, forfeiting it all once caught. Even a walnut of stake compounds across clones until the total cost swamps any gain, making the attack self-defeating.
